key: Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; And, ye that are near, acknowledge My might.
s: Between God’s rising against the peoples and the fear of Zion’s sinners, the chapter turns to its hearers; Rashi, on 33:13, reads the near as penitents newly drawn close, the far as those faithful from their youth, and Radak, on 33:13, takes the near as those in the Assyrian camp, made to know the might that struck them.

evidence.gloss: [Rashi, on 33:13, ‘far off’:] those who believe in Me and do My will from their youth … [‘near’:] penitents who have drawn near to Me anew … [Radak, on 33:13, ‘Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done’:] in the camp of the king of Assyria; those far off will hear, and those near, who were in the Assyrian camp, will know the might of God, who prevailed over them and struck them.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Isaiah 33:13, at [366,13]); one unit, no dash. Plain sense faithful: 33:10 “Now will I arise, saith the LORD”, 33:12 the peoples burned as lime, 33:14 the sinners in Zion are afraid; the verse addresses the far and the near; no four-word repeat of the key. Rashi on 33:13: the far are those who believe in God and do His will from their youth, the near are penitents newly drawn close; Radak on 33:13: what God did in the camp of the king of Assyria, the far will hear, and the near, who were in that camp, will know the might of God that prevailed over them and struck them (Metzudat David agrees with Radak). The two genuinely differ and are named without resolving. The proposer’s gloss mis-parsed Radak’s opening phrase slightly; the sentence itself is faithful, and the gloss here is corrected.
